title: Adora Compiler: End-to-End Optimization for High-Efficiency Dataflow Acceleration and Task Pipelining on CGRAs
problem: CGRAs are energy-efficient for nested-loop workloads but lack a user-friendly compiler; existing tools cannot automatically map loop algorithms to dataflow + task-pipelining, limiting CGRA adoption.
method: Compiler with CGRA-specific loop transformations for dataflow mapping, task-pipelining optimization across loops, and automated algorithm for end-to-end scheduling; produces high-utilization mappings on CGRA SoCs with minimal user intervention.

title: Be CIM or Be Memory: A Dual-mode-aware DNN Compiler for CIM Accelerators
problem: CIM accelerators can dynamically switch between compute mode and memory mode, but existing DNN compilers ignore this capability and statically assign resources, leaving performance on the table especially for LLMs with diverse memory and compute demands. No existing compilation framework models or optimizes the compute-memory mode switch in CIM hardware.
method: CMSwitch introduces a new hardware abstraction attribute that exposes the compute-memory mode switch to the compiler optimization space. A compilation optimization pass uses dynamic programming and mixed-integer programming (MIP) to identify the optimal network segment boundaries and mode-resource allocations. A tailored meta-operator expresses the compiled result in a generalized manner that maps across different CIM hardware targets.

title: Millimeter-Sized 0.1pM LoD Wireless 16-Channel Organic-Electrochemical-Transistor-Based Electrochemical Sensing SoC
problem: Miniaturized electrochemical sensor implants for long-term biomarker monitoring face challenges in achieving high sensitivity, wide dynamic range, and spatial resolution while remaining small enough for implantation; traditional three-electrode (3E) systems and ISFETs suffer from low scalability and limited channel integration.
method: The millimeter-scale SoC integrates 16 channels of organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) for direct biomarker sensing with wireless readout, replacing conventional 3E/ISFET approaches to enable higher scalability and reduced system size while managing OECT high static current demands through optimized sensor interface design.

title: Espresso: Exploiting the Sparsity Property in Event Sensors with Spatiotemporal Ordering
problem: Event-based vision sensors generate sparse high-speed event streams, but efficient stream processing without destroying sparsity properties is architecturally challenging.
method: Espresso designs an FPGA-based architecture for event-based vision that efficiently processes spatiotemporal event streams while maintaining sparsity. Uses ordered data structures and specialized compute patterns to avoid materializing dense representations.

title: Late Breaking Results: Decentralized Voting-Based Attestation for IoT Devices
problem: Traditional remote attestation (RA) schemes for IoT rely on a single trusted verifier, creating a single point of failure and security vulnerability.
method: Proposes voting-based blockchain attestation protocol where distributed verification occurs across all nodes, creating immutable traceable attestation history accessible to auditors.

title: ReChisel: Effective Automatic Chisel Code Generation by LLM with Reflection
problem: Chisel (high-level HDL based on Scala) enables more concise and maintainable hardware designs than Verilog, but LLM-based Chisel code generation remains unexplored despite growing interest in LLM-assisted HDL coding.
method: ReChisel is an LLM-based agentic system incorporating reflection mechanism to iteratively refine generated Chisel code using feedback from compilation and simulation. Includes escape mechanism to break free from non-progress loops, enabling multi-round refinement until correct code is produced.

title: 35.3 A 30MHz Wideband 92.7dB SNR 99.6% Accuracy Bioimpedance Spectroscopy IC Using Time-to-Digital Demodulation with Co-Prime Delay Locked Sampling
problem: Wideband bioimpedance spectroscopy up to 30MHz requires high SNR (>90dB) and phase accuracy (<0.6°) for biological assessment (fluid volume, cancer diagnosis, plant composition), but existing ICs are limited to 10MHz with analog I-Q demodulation suffering from 4+ degree phase errors.
method: The IC employs time-to-digital (T-D) demodulation instead of conventional I-Q mixing, achieving phase accuracy through: (1) co-prime delay-locked (CDL) sampling with 21.6GHz equivalent sampling rate from 240MHz clock via delay-locking techniques; (2) compact phase comparator-based DLL for high-accuracy delay generation; (3) optimized wideband current generator and front-end design. Eliminates analog multiplication distortion.

title: RESCQ: Realtime Scheduling for Continuous Angle Quantum Error Correction Architectures
problem: Continuous angle quantum error correction architectures require non-deterministic resource state production, meaning statically generated schedules waste cycles when states fail and must be re-attempted. Without a realtime scheduler, execution time is unnecessarily long and classical control overhead for frequent rescheduling can dominate.
method: RESCQ is a realtime scheduler for continuous angle QEC architectures that actively redistributes resources on-demand based on expected production rates of rotation states. It monitors resource state generation success and, upon failure, dynamically reassigns resources from lower-priority to higher-priority operations to minimize total cycle count. To control classical control overhead, RESCQ adaptively selects the recomputation frequency based on the state of the system, reducing unnecessary scheduling invocations when the system is stable.

title: Scaling All-to-All Operations Across Emerging Many-Core Supercomputers
problem: Existing all-to-all MPI algorithms don't fully exploit many-core supercomputer architectures; performance varies with message size and process count
method: Novel all-to-all algorithms designed for many-core supercomputers with optimization for message size and process count variations

title: 20.1 A 3.5×3.5mm2 1.47mW/ch 16-Channel MSS-CMOS Heterogeneous Multi-Modal-Gas-Sensor Chip Stack
problem: Miniaturized multi-channel gas sensors with low power are needed for wearables, ingestible biomedical devices, and smart tags, but traditional gas sensors separate transducers from CMOS via wiring, requiring large packaging; prior MEMS-CMOS stacks lack multi-gas capability and scalability.
method: Heterogeneous MEMS-CMOS stack integrating Membrane-type Surface-stress Sensor (MSS) transducers on top of CMOS analog frontend and digital readout; 16-channel architecture with 1.47mW/channel power on 3.5×3.5mm2 footprint.

title: UB-mesh: An New Interconnection Technology for Large AI SuperNode
problem: Scaling AI clusters with many GPUs requires very-high-bandwidth, low-latency interconnects; current PCIe and traditional switch fabrics limit all-to-all communication for distributed training.
method: UB-mesh proposes a custom mesh-topology interconnect optimized for GPU clusters. It likely includes novel switching logic, reduced hop counts, and optimized link speeds compared to traditional Ethernet/Infiniband.

title: MISA-AKMC : Achieve Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulation of 20 Quadrillion Atoms on GPU Clusters
problem: Atomic Kinetic Monte Carlo requires massive memory for large-scale simulations; porting to GPUs faces memory pressure and communication overhead scaling limitations
method: GPU cluster implementation with Lattice Data Compression and Vacancy Decompression algorithms; multi-level pipeline with on-demand communication merging reduces data transfer

title: Principle-based Dataflow Optimization for Communication Lower Bound in Operator-Fused Tensor Accelerator
problem: Design space exploration for tensor accelerator dataflows is time-consuming and lacks architectural insight; optimal memory communication bounds for fused operators are not well characterized.
method: Proposes principles for dataflow optimization that provide communication lower bounds for tensor operators; derives optimal tiling, scheduling, mapping for intra/inter-operator dataflow; introduces FuseCU architecture supporting profitable operator fusion.

title: Scalable, High-Fidelity Monitoring of Application Communication Patterns in Vernier
problem: Understanding irregular, dynamic HPC application communication patterns at scale is critical for optimization and architecture evaluation. Current approaches are either too coarse (aggregated statistics) or too detailed (exhaustive traces), creating scalability and flexibility trade-offs.
method: Vernier system with configurable histogram-based communication monitoring. Collects statistical data (not traces) about annotated communication patterns. Enables online/offline analysis, benchmarking, network simulation.

title: Enhancing ChatPORT with CUDA-to-SYCL Kernel Translation Capability
problem: Code translation for parallel programming models (CUDA to SYCL) remains largely unexplored despite LLMs' general code translation capabilities
method: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of 19 open-source code models (0.5-34B params) on CUDA-to-SYCL kernel pairs from heterogeneous computing benchmarks

title: BROCA: A Low-power and Low-latency Conversational Agent RISC-V System-on-Chip for Voice-interactive Mobile Devices
problem: Mobile voice assistants require on-device AI inference with sub-100ms latency and minimal power consumption; BROCA targets running conversational agent models (speech recognition + NLU + TTS) entirely on mobile SoC.
method: BROCA implements a RISC-V SoC with specialized accelerators for speech processing (DSP-like vector units), low-latency AI inference (likely quantized transformer acceleration), and integrated audio I/O, optimized for the speech-to-speech latency critical to voice interaction.
